events.subject: Welcome to the team
body: Good work on Northgate. That warning had sat in the register for fourteen months and you were the first person to ask why.

A few things about how we work here. Your inbox will fill up: incidents, requests, the odd favour. Some need a reply within a week or two, and if you leave them, someone else decides for you. Not everything is urgent. Learn which is which.
events.headline: Valtren Coldline reports record pharma volumes

events.subject: Fellow survivor of induction week
body: Hi, Callum. We started the same week. I'm on the KRI dashboards and the monthly pack.
Celeste Marlow stopped by my desk yesterday asking who did the Northgate work. I said it was you. You're welcome. Fancy splitting the fleet data pull this week? It's a pig of a job.

choices.label: Split the data pull with him
choices.outcome: You spend two late evenings on it together. Callum is sharper than he lets on, and he owes you one.

choices.label: Politely decline: you have your own deadlines
choices.outcome: Callum shrugs. "Fair. Offer stands."

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Callum does the pull on his own and mentions to Priya, lightly, that you were too busy to help.

events.subject: Thursday?
events.body: I booked that Lebanese place for Thursday, 7:30. You promised. Don't make me eat the mezze alone.

choices.label: Go, phone off
choices.outcome: A good evening. You talk about something other than work for three hours.

choices.label: Go, but take the laptop for after
choices.outcome: You are there, mostly. Sam notices the bag by the door.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: You forgot. Sam ate the mezze alone and sent a photo of the empty chair.

events.subject: Probably nothing
body: Odd one. I was at Harrowgate late on Tuesday finishing the flood walk-through, and Celeste came out of the site office at nine with a man I didn't know. Expensive coat, Corvane lanyard.
No procurement people, no meeting in the diary. Probably nothing. You're the one who likes loose threads.

choices.label: Thank him and write it down
choices.outcome: You note the date, the site and the name on the lanyard. It goes into a file you have not labelled yet.

choices.label: Ask him what else he noticed
choices.outcome: Callum remembers more than he said: the Corvane man was the managing director, and Celeste walked him to his car. You write it all down.

choices.label: Tell him executives meet suppliers all the time
choices.outcome: "Sure," says Callum. He does not bring it up again.

events.subject: Coffee?
body: I've read your last three pieces of work. Clear, practical, no jargon. We need more of that.
I'd like to mentor you, informally. Thirty minutes a fortnight. People who have a sponsor at the top move faster here; I would rather it was someone who deserves it.

choices.label: Accept gratefully
choices.outcome: Celeste is generous with her time and her contacts. Hollis notices whose coffees you are drinking.

choices.label: Accept, and tell Priya you're doing it
choices.outcome: Priya raises an eyebrow, then nods. "Keep your notes and your independence."

choices.label: Thank her but keep your distance
choices.outcome: "Of course." Her reply is warm. The next one, a month later, is shorter.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Celeste does not chase. She also does not forget.

events.subject: Nice work on the fleet indicators
body: Hollis loved the fatigue indicators in the monthly pack. Callum presented them very well.
I had assumed they were yours. Were they?

choices.label: Explain calmly what you built and what Callum added
choices.outcome: Priya thanks you. In the next pack, the authorship line has both names. Callum is cooler with you for a while.

choices.label: Go and have it out with Callum first
choices.outcome: A tense conversation by the coffee machine. He apologises, sort of. Half the floor heard.

choices.label: Let it go: the work matters, not the name
choices.outcome: Priya lets it drop. Callum's name is the one Hollis remembers.

events.subject: Truce, and a tip
body: We've been competing for two years and frankly it's exhausting. So: a tip. Procurement has been asked to 'tidy up' the supplier approvals log before the auditors' visit. Asked by the COO's office.
I didn't tell you this.

choices.label: Ask Internal Audit to take a copy of the log today
choices.outcome: Audit takes a full extract that afternoon. Two days later, the live log is 'reorganised'. The extract is safe.

choices.label: Thank him and keep watching
choices.outcome: You keep an eye on the log. When you next look, several entries have moved.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: The log is tidied. Callum stops sharing.

events.subject: Re: that supplier name you asked about
body: You asked whether Compliance had ever done due diligence on Tessaline Haulage Services. We haven't. It was onboarded under the operational emergency route, so it never came to us.
If you want to look it up yourself, the company registry is public. I'd keep a note of when you looked and what you found.

choices.label: Look it up and file a dated note
choices.outcome: One director: D. Marlow. Registered address: a flat above a dry cleaner's. No vehicles registered. You sit very still for a minute.

choices.label: Ask Ruth to run formal due diligence
choices.outcome: Ruth runs it properly and copies Internal Audit. The registry entry comes back with her signature on the file note.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: It slides down the list. Ruth assumes you lost interest.

events.subject: Comment request: Valtren suppliers
body: I'm Jonah Pike at the Courier. I'm working on a piece about procurement at regional logistics firms and Valtren's name keeps coming up, specifically a supplier called Corvane.
I'd value a conversation, on background. My number is below.

choices.label: Refer him to the press office and tell Ruth
choices.outcome: The press office sends a holding line. Ruth logs the contact. You keep the investigation where it belongs, inside.

choices.label: Talk to him on background
choices.outcome: You say less than you know and more than you should. Jonah is grateful. It feels like lighting a fuse.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Jonah tries twice more, then stops.

events.subject: Can we talk? Not here.
events.body: I think you know what I know. I've kept copies. I need to know whether you'll protect the people who give you evidence, or whether this goes the way it went last time.

choices.label: Meet him, and walk him through the protected speak-up route
choices.outcome: Tomasz files through the speak-up line to the Audit Committee Chair, with his copies attached. He looks ten years younger walking out.

choices.label: Meet him in a cafe and take his copies yourself
choices.outcome: You get the copies. You also become the only person who can vouch for where they came from.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Tomasz takes your silence as an answer.

events.subject: A word of advice
body: I hear you've been asking about our supplier arrangements. Supplier strategy is an operational matter and it is mine.
You have a bright future here. I'd hate to see it spent on a misunderstanding.

choices.label: Reply that you're doing routine assurance work
choices.outcome: "Good," she writes. Your access to two procurement folders is quietly removed the next day.

choices.label: Forward it to Dame Helen as a pressure attempt
choices.outcome: Dame Helen replies within the hour: "Noted. Carry on. Keep everything."

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Silence is also an answer. Celeste reads it correctly.

events.subject: Are you OK?
events.body: You were up at 3 again. You check your phone in the shower. I'm not angry, I'm worried. Can we take a weekend? Just one.

choices.label: Take the weekend, properly
choices.outcome: Two days on the coast, phone in a drawer. You come back lighter.

choices.label: Promise a weekend after this crunch
choices.outcome: Sam says "OK" in the way that means it isn't.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Sam stops asking. That is worse.

events.subject: Weekend cover?
events.body: Ops have asked for risk cover on the peak weekend in case anything goes sideways at the depots. It's voluntary. I can't pay overtime, but people notice who turns up.

choices.label: Cover the weekend
choices.outcome: A quiet weekend, mostly. You spot a reefer unit drifting warm on Saturday night and get it swapped before a load is lost.

choices.label: Propose a fair rota across the team
choices.outcome: Priya likes it and it becomes the norm. You do one shift in four.

choices.label: Decline: you've promised the weekend at home
choices.outcome: "Totally fine," says Priya, and means it.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Someone else covers. Priya wonders why you didn't answer.

events.subject: Your dad's in hospital
events.body: Nothing life-threatening, a fall, but they're keeping him in for tests. Your mum is in a state. Can you get away?

choices.label: Go today and tell Priya
choices.outcome: Priya covers your week without a second thought. Your dad is fine. Your mum holds your hand the whole time.

choices.label: Go at the weekend after the board paper
choices.outcome: You make it on Saturday. Your dad jokes that you look worse than he does.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Sam goes on their own and phones you from the ward. The silence on the line is long.

events.subject: A headhunter called the house
events.body: Someone from a recruitment firm called the landline asking for you. Something about a Head of Risk job at Penhallow Chill Freight, more money, fewer hours. I said you'd call back. Will you?

choices.label: Decline: you have unfinished business at Valtren
choices.outcome: You call back and say no. It feels good to know someone asked.

choices.label: Mention it to Priya
choices.outcome: Priya says she hopes you'll stay and that she'll make the case for your development budget. Hollis approves it within a week.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: The headhunter moves on to the next name.

events.subject: Your flood numbers
events.body: That Harrowgate appraisal was the first risk paper I've read this year that I could actually take to the board. If you ever need a budget argument made properly, my door is open.

events.subject: Need you on side for Monday
body: Monday's exec meeting decides whether we bid for the national pharma distribution tender. Hollis will say we can't staff it. I say we can't afford not to.
A word from risk saying the operational risks are manageable would carry the room. Can I count on you?

choices.label: Back the bid as manageable
choices.outcome: The bid goes in. Rafe calls you 'one of the good ones'. Hollis looks at you for a long second.

choices.label: Support it only with staffing conditions agreed first
choices.outcome: The bid goes in with a staffing plan and a go/no-go gate. Both sides grumble, which usually means it was right.

choices.label: Side with Hollis: not this year
choices.outcome: The bid is dropped. Rafe tells the CEO the risk function 'killed the deal'.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: The decision is made without the risk view. Nobody remembers to ask next time either.

events.subject: Town hall: a question for risk
events.body: At Friday's town hall I want someone from risk to answer a staff question live: 'Are we growing faster than it's safe to?' I'd like the answer to be reassuring.

choices.label: Answer honestly: where growth is safe and where it isn't
choices.outcome: The room goes quiet, then applauds. Adrian thanks you through slightly tight teeth.

choices.label: Give the reassuring answer he wants
choices.outcome: Adrian is pleased. On the front line, someone types 'told you so' into the speak-up line.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Callum answers instead.

events.subject: Unannounced inspection: Corby Road
events.body: The Authority will carry out an unannounced inspection of temperature monitoring at Corby Road this week. Please nominate a contact and make records available.
events.headline: Cold chain regulator inspects Valtren depot

choices.label: Give full access and declare the known gaps up front
choices.outcome: Imogen finds two minor issues, both already in your action tracker. Her report notes 'a self-aware control environment'.

choices.label: Provide exactly what is asked and no more
choices.outcome: The inspection finds a logger gap you knew about. Imogen asks why it wasn't mentioned. Fine: 40,000.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: The inspector arrives to find no nominated contact. The report criticises governance. Fine: 90,000.

events.subject: Information request: excursion data
events.body: Under our supervisory powers we request all temperature excursion records for the last twelve months, with root causes and actions, within ten working days.

choices.label: Send complete records with your own analysis
choices.outcome: Imogen's reply is two lines: 'Received. This is what good looks like.'

choices.label: Ask for an extension to clean the data
choices.outcome: Granted, with a note on file about data quality.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: The deadline passes. The Authority opens an enforcement review.

events.subject: Supervisory letter
events.body: Following our recent engagement, the Authority has moved Valtren Coldline Logistics to standard supervision. We note in particular the quality of the risk function's self-identified issues.
events.headline: Regulator eases supervision of Valtren after governance review

events.subject: We need to talk about the incidents
body: Three incidents in a few months, and Internal Audit has noticed that most trace back to calls the risk team signed off.
I'm not looking for a scapegoat. I want us to show we learn. What do you want to do?

choices.label: Run an honest lessons-learned review, your own calls included
choices.outcome: The review is uncomfortable and useful. Two controls change. Audit closes its query.

choices.label: Argue the incidents were bad luck
choices.outcome: Some were. Audit notes that 'luck' appears in three of the four explanations.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Audit writes its own review. Your name is in it.

events.subject: The yard is unhappy
events.body: Morale on the night shifts is the lowest I've seen. Two good shift leaders resigned last week. People say management only listens after something goes wrong.

choices.label: Do a night walk-round with Grace and listen
choices.outcome: You hear about broken heaters, a rota nobody can live with and a near miss nobody reported. You fix the first two that week.

choices.label: Ask HR for a survey
choices.outcome: The survey goes out. Response rate: 12%.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Another shift leader resigns.

events.subject: Your paper
events.body: I read your paper twice, which I rarely do. It told me something I did not already know and was honest about what you did not know. Please keep writing like that, whoever asks you not to.

events.subject: Backup budget, again
events.body: My request to test the offline backups was cut for the third year running. If ransomware hits, I genuinely don't know if we can restore. Would you put it in your risk report?

choices.label: Put it in the report with a cost of not doing it
choices.outcome: Hollis funds a restore test. It fails the first time, which is exactly why you test.

choices.label: Note it as a watch item
choices.outcome: It sits in the watch list, amber, for another year.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Mei stops asking you.

events.subject: Heatwave next month?
events.body: Long-range forecast shows a heatwave in about six weeks. Last time we lost three reefer units in a day. Do you want me to pre-book spare units?

choices.label: Pre-book spares and brief the depots
choices.outcome: Spares on standby, depots briefed. Amara sends a thumbs-up and a sun emoji.

choices.label: Wait for a firmer forecast
choices.outcome: Reasonable. The forecast firms up, and so do the prices.

choices.label: (No reply)
choices.outcome: Amara books two units out of her own budget and doesn't mention it again.

events.subject: Rival haulier loses pharma licence
events.body: Penhallow Chill Freight has had its pharmaceutical distribution licence suspended after repeated temperature excursions. Clients are looking for alternatives.
events.headline: Penhallow Chill Freight loses pharma licence; clients look elsewhere

events.subject: Energy prices climb
events.body: Wholesale electricity prices are up 18% this quarter. Cold stores are among the hardest hit.
events.headline: Energy prices up 18%: cold store operators squeezed

events.subject: Valtren under pressure
events.body: Analysts question whether Valtren's controls have kept up with its growth after a string of incidents.
events.headline: Analysts question Valtren's controls after string of incidents

events.subject: Valtren wins industry award
events.body: Valtren Coldline Logistics has been named regional logistics firm of the year, with judges citing its 'mature approach to risk'.
events.headline: Valtren named logistics firm of the year for 'mature approach to risk'

events.subject: Courier: questions over Valtren supplier
events.body: The Brindlemoor Courier reports that a Valtren supplier paid rebates to a company linked to a senior executive.
events.headline: Courier: Valtren supplier paid rebates to firm linked to executive

events.subject: Valtren COO steps down
events.body: Valtren Coldline Logistics announced that its Chief Operating Officer has left the company with immediate effect following an Audit Committee investigation into supplier payments.
events.headline: Valtren COO steps down after Audit Committee investigation

fallout.headline: Valtren hit by avoidable operational failure

fallout.description: A load was lost at a depot. The investigation traced it to the approach agreed in "{mission}" ("{choice}").
fallout.headline: Valtren loses temperature-sensitive load at depot

fallout.description: An audit adjustment landed on a number the risk team signed off in "{mission}" ("{choice}").
fallout.headline: Valtren restates provision after audit review

fallout.description: The regulator flagged a weakness that goes back to "{mission}" ("{choice}").
fallout.headline: Regulator raises concerns over Valtren compliance

fallout.description: A security alert went unhandled for a day. The gap traces back to "{mission}" ("{choice}").
fallout.headline: Valtren systems disrupted by security incident

fallout.description: A near-miss in the yard became an injury. The review points to "{mission}" ("{choice}").
fallout.headline: Worker injured at Valtren depot

fallout.description: A supplier problem landed without warning. The contract terms agreed in "{mission}" ("{choice}") left no protection.
fallout.headline: Supplier problems hit Valtren deliveries

fallout.description: The board asked why a risk flagged in "{mission}" was handled the way it was ("{choice}"). The answer did not satisfy them.
fallout.headline: Valtren board questions risk oversight
